Read `README.md` and current rollout evidence first. Produce exactly one multi-wake target-policy candidate in `solver/`. Keep candidate-specific reasoning in `logs/optimize/wake_policy_notes.md`, and add or materially revise at least one evidence-backed reusable lesson in `guidance/control_experience.md` from the assigned parent, sampled solver results, and inherited logs. If no positive lesson survives the evidence, record a concrete negative result and what later workers should avoid or test. The candidate is incomplete until both files are updated. Work only inside this Phase 2 workspace.

Use the fish-control bookshelf through this structured transfer protocol:

1. Before the first architecture proposal from the common naive seed, consult `guidance/skills/fish-control-primitives/SKILL.md` and its references.
2. On later iterations, consult it again when the inherited guidance indicates three consecutive completed iterations with neither a new controller mechanism nor a semantic improvement such as a new success, a better termination class, or a meaningfully different useful trajectory.
3. Consultation is required at those moments; adopting a primitive is optional. Do not use the shelf to justify scalar-only gain tuning.
4. If a source informs the edit, record a concise block in `logs/optimize/wake_policy_notes.md`:

```text
bookshelf_consulted: true
source_domain:
source_mechanism:
transferable_invariant:
nontransferable_details:
policy_translation:
falsification:
```

Translate only the invariant into normalized body-frame observations and the two-joint state-feedback contract. Prefer one mechanism or one small compatible combination. Published gains, species-specific kinematics, exact vortex phases, and task-specific routes are not transferable answers.

I’ll first read the workspace contract, then the fish-control shelf and the required wake-visual inspection instructions. After that I’ll trace the assigned parent and inherited rollout evidence before touching the single candidate.

The workspace requires a visual diagnosis before any policy edit, plus a durable guidance change and a final contract check. I’m now mapping the parent candidate, sampled guidance, inherited notes, and all four evidence bundles so the architecture choice is grounded in comparisons rather than score alone.

The evidence confirms direct uniform still-water initialization, so the visuals are admissible. The raw diagnostics contain full per-step records; I’m extracting only trajectory/control summaries and will inspect the compact combined sheets directly, with special attention to the best near approach (`4.128 L`) versus the more coherent but less direct trajectories.

The visual/control cross-check isolates the parent failure: the course-feedback candidate barely propelled (`0.024 L` closest progress by the inherited summary), curled upward, and exited at `8.65 T`; its speed-gated course signal became influential while the geometric bearing was already crossing centerline. I’m now consulting the required fish-control shelf for a mechanism that separates slow steering bias from the fast propulsive cycle—this consultation is mandatory before the architecture proposal.

The shelf points to one clean mechanism supported by the observed failure: keep the proven state-feedback traveling bend, remove course/yaw-rate mean-curvature feedback, and steer by smoothly strengthening one observed posterior half-cycle according to body-frame bearing. This should create a signed cycle-mean bend without replacing propulsion with a static offset. I’ll record that visual diagnosis and falsification criteria now, before editing the candidate as required by the wake-visual skill.

The single candidate is now implemented, and the parent guidance has a concrete negative boundary for the failed course/yaw-to-static-curvature design. The new policy changes the steering primitive—not just gains—and keeps every active parameter in `target_policy_params`. Next I’m validating syntax, schema, reflection behavior, and the mandated checker contract; no CFD will be run here.

The mandated checker file specifies three lightweight checks and no CFD. I’m invoking its dedicated check-runner now; while it validates, I’ll independently inspect the candidate’s symmetry/zero-error behavior and file-scope diff so any failure can be repaired promptly.

A supplemental command used solver-relative paths incorrectly and also exposed that `julia` is not on this shell’s current `PATH`; it did not test or modify the candidate. I’m correcting the path check now, while the dedicated runner follows the workspace’s prescribed environment and will determine whether this is merely shell setup or an actual validation blocker.

The mandated runner reports the substantive checks passing: guidance semantic change PASS and solver boundary PASS. Its contract check is blocked solely because no `julia` executable is on `PATH`, not by a policy assertion. I’m exhausting workspace-safe runtime locations and will rerun the same contract test with an available Julia binary if one exists.

Julia is available through the evaluation runtime path. The policy now passes a supplemental finite-output and reflection-equivariance test exactly. I’m also checking the isolated two-joint dynamics (without CFD) to confirm that zero bearing recovers the symmetric gait and opposite bearings produce opposite, bounded cycle-mean posterior bias.

The isolated gait check hit an overly tight `0.2°` numerical mean threshold before printing results; this is a test-threshold failure, not a controller exception. I’m rerunning over an integer number of nominal cycles and will judge symmetry by paired zero/opposite-bearing results and the actual joint envelope.

All three mandated checks now pass after adding the existing Julia runtime directory to `PATH`. The extra free-joint integration was intentionally outside the episode and omitted its hard joint-angle/speed constraints, so its long-horizon envelope is not a valid policy check; I’m discarding that result and using the real sampled constrained trajectories plus the passing contract instead. One final audit will confirm the exact file scope and evidence-backed notes.

Implemented one 3D target-policy candidate using bearing-gated posterior half-cycle asymmetry while preserving the traveling-wave oscillator:

- [candidate_target_policy.jl](solver/cases/dogfish_3d_shape_policy/candidate_target_policy.jl:1)
- [wake_policy_notes.md](logs/optimize/wake_policy_notes.md:1)
- [control_experience.md](guidance/control_experience.md:89)

The mandated check-runner passed:

- Guidance semantic-change check
- Julia policy contract and parameter-schema check
- Solver boundary/edit-scope check

Supplemental finite-output and reflection-equivariance checks also passed. No CFD was run.
